replay: recorded windows re-judged under the exclusion rule (contended/sparse never enter the decision sample)
why: the clean run predates the rule, so its published verdict had to be re-derived from its own recorded windows rather than assumed still valid

clean_run_12_53.interpretation: every window was quiet, so the exclusion rule removes nothing and the published verdict stands. This is the formal performance evidence.

8192x4096.note: the old rules judged it FAIL on a sample with no quiet reference at all

contended_run_13_03.interpretation: 9 of 9 windows were contended, so nothing is left to decide on. The old code still returned FAIL; that was the defect this rule repairs. The run is kept as the witness validation experiment only, never as a performance conclusion.

exclusion_reverted_on_purpose.conclusion: the guard is load-bearing, not decorative: reverting the implementation breaks the tests that claim to protect it

contamination_probe.setup: 15 quiet windows at 1.02x plus 5 contended at 0.20x (75% quiet, so the gate passes)
contamination_probe.conclusion: with the gate satisfied the verdict is still computed from quiet windows only, so a contended arm cannot drag the median

branch_reachability.fixed: the unusable-shortfall check now runs BEFORE the quiet rules; sample is a subset of usable, so in the old order that branch could never be reached

wash_to_pass_arithmetic.conclusion: a candidate twice as slow would clear the MATCH lower bound if contended windows were allowed into the sample
